headline_marked: [[Claude Desktop and Cursor actually watch videos]] with fully local MCP support
headline: Claude Desktop and Cursor actually watch videos with fully local MCP support
summary: A new MIT-licensed tool, claude-real-video (1.9k stars), enables Claude Desktop and Cursor to process videos locally. It extracts scene-aware keyframes and transcripts for efficient AI analysis.
details: The open-source project claude-real-video (MIT, 1.9k stars) now allows AI agents like Claude Desktop and Cursor to "watch" videos. It extracts scene-aware, deduplicated keyframes and a timestamped transcript from any video URL or local file, with all processing done on your machine.

Since version 0.8.0, claude-real-video ships as an MCP (Multi-Client Protocol) server. This means MCP clients, including Cursor, can directly request video analysis using a standard stdio command, `crv-mcp`.

The tool uses scene detection to identify and extract only the frames that truly differ, avoiding wasted context on near-identical frames and ensuring fast cuts are not missed. This method significantly reduces the number of tokens required for analysis; a 58-second clip can go from 58 sampled frames to 26 relevant ones.

Analyses are cached per source under `~/.cache/crv-mcp`, making follow-up questions about the same video instant. The repository's benchmark folder provides reproducible comparisons demonstrating the efficiency gains.
caption:
